item.title: What's gone up even faster than gas or rent? The cost of caregiving
item.description: A new study from AARP shows caregivers' out-of-pocket costs rose about 60% in the last five years.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Israel's election too close to call. And, the Ebola outbreak reaches grim milestone
item.description: Israeli voters turned out in record numbers, and the results remain too close to call. And, more than 10,000 people have been infected with Ebola since the outbreak was first declared in May.

item.title: At least 30 dead in crash between two trains in central Spain, media say
item.description: A high-speed train slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped, derailing two cars and killing at least 30 people on Wednesday in central Spain, according to local media.
item.content:encoded:
A high-speed train slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped, derailing two cars and killing at least 30 people on Wednesday in central Spain, according to local media.

(Image credit: Juanma Jiménez)

item.title: How a lifelong Republican came to lead the data center battle in Ohio
item.description: In Ohio, many people are displeased with the state's rapid buildout of data centers. It's a hot issue in the midterms, as political candidates from both parties try to ease voter concerns.

item.title: Why many student voters have a right to choose where to register to vote
item.description: Student voters studying outside their hometown have a right to choose where they register to vote. Advocates say a Montana legal fight is a reminder of a misunderstanding of those students' rights.

item.title: Partnerships between ICE and local police surge, report finds
item.description: The number of state and local officers working with Immigration and Customs Enforcement has doubled in size in the last eight months, according to a new report from the immigration reform advocacy group FWD.us.

item.title: Are you an organ donor? Here are some rule changes you may want to know
item.description: Transplant teams can talk to families about organ donation before they've decided whether to continue life-sustaining medical care for loved ones. Until now, that has been forbidden.
